column1: # boru Language Specification: the boru:parselang module + the core `parse` word
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# `parse <kind> <opts?> <source>` is the sibling of `mini`: it expands at the
# call site to the STANDARD parser call `ParseLang.parse_<kind> <source> <opts>
# end`. Unlike `mini`, the `source` is the REQUIRED LAST surface arg (a String
# or a {src:…} Source map) and `opts` is the optional MIDDLE one — disambiguated
# by arity. A parser returns Any (an AST, a transduction, …). The kind set is
# FIXED (the tabnas family + aontu); a custom parser is a Function VALUE (§10;
# `ParseLang.register` is a tombstone raising parse_registry_frozen).
# `ParseLang.kinds` lists the kinds; `ParseLang.source` resolves a source value
# to its String. These rows def-bind a small `calc` parser fn whose AST is the
# token list `[left op right]` (built by StringUtil.split on the resolved
# source). A {file:…} source is deferred in v1.
# §1  parse — a def-bound boru parser fn returning a tokenization
import "boru:parselang"  import "boru:string-util"  def calc (fn [[source:Any opts:Map] [List] [StringUtil.split ' ' (ParseLang.source source)]])  end  (parse calc 'x + y') get 1
column3: the parsed operator token

column1: # §9  aontu — the built-in aontu parser, the upstream Go port of
#     github.com/rjrodger/aontu (the repo's go/ module), a CUE-inspired
#     unification config dialect. It parses, unifies and generates the source
#     to a Node of Maps and Lists: top-level `k:v` entries and the colon-chain
#     `a:b:c:1` build maps, `[…]` builds lists, duplicate keys and `&`
#     deep-merge, bare kind words (string/number/integer/boolean/top) constrain
#     scalars, an absolute `$.a` reference resolves from the root and a relative
#     `.k` reference resolves a sibling key at the current map level.
import "boru:parselang"  (parse aontu 'a:1 b:2') get 'b'
column3: top-level key/value entries build a Map

column1: import "boru:parselang"  (((parse aontu 'a:b:c:1') get 'a') get 'b') get 'c'
column3: the colon-chain a:b:c:1 nests Maps

column1: import "boru:parselang"  ((parse aontu 'a:[10,20,30]') get 'a') get 1
column3: a [list] builds a List; elements may be comma- or space-separated

column1: import "boru:parselang"  ((parse aontu 'a:{b:1} a:{c:2}') get 'a') get 'c'
column3: duplicate keys deep-merge their Maps (unification)

column3: a kind word unifies with a matching scalar to yield the scalar

column3: an absolute $ reference resolves from the document root

column1: # §10  a ParseLang VALUE as the parser — `parse <fn> <opts?> <source>`. The
#      first operand may BE the parser: a Function (or a word bound to one)
#      whose every signature starts with the standard [source opts] prefix —
#      the same contract ParseLang.register enforces. The call expands to the
#      direct fn call `<fn> <source> <opts> end` with no kind lookup, so a
#      parser works without being registered under a kind name. A registered
#      kind wins a name collision. A parser COMPUTED by a runtime call —
#      `parse (mk) 'x'` — compiles through the recorded parselang-fn-dispatch:
#      the fn operand's producing event is its provenance.
import "boru:parselang"  (parse (ParseLang.parse_json) '{"b":7}') get 'b'
column3: a module-exported parser used as a ParseLang value

column3: a word bound to a parser fn is the value form spelled by name
